Touch me not! I am Red Death stalking!
Good evening. You are new here. Be careful where you walk in this house.

Who are you? You are standing in my light.
M. Richard, the manager

M. Moncharmin, the manager
Good evening. You haven't seen anything odd tonight, I hope?
A pleasant evening to you. It is our last night, thank heaven.
We are leaving. And not a moment too soon, between ourselves.
M. Mercier, the acting-manager
No time, no time! The managers want me, the stage wants me ...
The managers are in conference. Can I take a message?
Gabriel, the chorus-master
Don't speak of him! Not here! Touch wood!
M. Mifroid, the commissary

Come in, come in. Christine's Angel? Oh, he's a good genius, I'm sure of it.
Box Five? I've been told to keep an eye on it.
Christine ... Christine ... you must love me!

The Persian's proofs
Paris, thirty years after it all. You are helping a writer who has been ransacking the archives of the Opera, the National Academy of Music, for the truth about its ghost. He is sure of it now.
The Persian, an old man now
👻 He really existed

The Opera ghost really existed. He was not, as was long believed, a creature of the imagination of the artists, the superstition of the managers, or a product of the absurd and impressionable brains of the young ladies of the ballet, their mothers, the box-keepers, the cloak-room attendants or the concierge.
